subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Happy to update if I missed anything.

Pain points you shared
- Rising per-token spend with current OpenAI usage, especially for embeddings and multi-turn chat.
- Lack of predictable performance and regional availability for your EU customers.
- Need for a safe, auditable migration path (security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence) and the ability to roll back if quality/regression appears.

Current stack and usage
- Primary providers: OpenAI (chat completions + embeddings) and Anthropic for safety-sensitive flows.
- Traffic: ~300k tokens/day (production), peak spikes to ~1M tokens/day during promos.
- Feature usage: streaming responses, function/tool-calling, embeddings for semantic search.
- Context window: typical prompts 2-4k tokens; some workflows need 8k+ context.

Success criteria (what "good" looks like)
- Cost: >=30% reduction in per-token inference cost at parity quality for core flows.
- Latency: p50 < 200ms and p95 < 700ms for single-turn chat responses at current throughput targets.
- Quality: classification/QA accuracy within ~5% of current OpenAI baseline on your eval set.
- Rollout: Pilot on 10% traffic, ramp to 50% with canary and automatic fallback to OpenAI/Anthropic on regressions.

Compatibility requirements
- Must support streaming and tool-calling semantics similar to OpenAI/Anthropic (webhook/tool invocation).
- Embeddings parity for semantic search vectors (same dimensionality or stable conversion path).
- Ability to run in EU region and in a private VPC for regulated datasets.

Initial model shortlist we discussed
- Llama 2 (higher-parameter variants for quality-critical flows)
- Mistral (strong few-shot performance)
- Falcon 40B (open, performant on long context)
- RedPajama / Open-weights-family for embeddings experiments

Next steps
1) You: share a sample of prompts and evaluation set (anonymized) — Emily
2) Us: run an initial quality/latency benchmark on shortlisted models and provide cost estimates — Marissa/Rishi
3) Legal/Security: we will send the SC questionnaire and NDA; please return the completed questionnaire (attached).
4) Schedule: propose a 60-min technical PoC kickoff next week to scope infra and data flow.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (basic timeline + owners), security_questionnaire.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to moving this ahead.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 17:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications/additions from our side: 

- Usage: OpenAI is used for both chat and embeddings (gpt-4.1 family for high-quality chat, ada-embedding/002 for vectors). Anthropic is used for compliance/sensitive content flows.
- Volume details: Production steady-state ~300k tokens/day, monthly average ~9M tokens. Peak day last quarter hit ~1.2M tokens.
- Latency: For a majority of user-facing interactions we target p50 < 150ms and p95 < 600ms; backend bulk embedding jobs can be higher.
- Security: We need to ensure KMS integration for key management and audit logs for embedding access.
- Success metrics: If you can demonstrate comparable quality for our search and QA flows and a clear regression testing plan, we'll greenlight a 6-week PoC.

Next steps on our side: I'll share an anonymized eval set and a short list of the top 20 prompts by traffic by end of day tomorrow. Also looping in our infra lead (cc'd internally) if we need specific network/VPC requirements.

Appreciate the thorough recap — Emily

Can you please: 
- Rishi: prepare an initial benchmark plan (models to test, quantization approach, target throughput) and an estimate for running the PoC in EU region.
- Aditya: prep a short doc on integration points (function calling + streaming + embeddings compatibility) and a minimal architecture for private deployment (VPC + KMS).

Let's aim to have the benchmark plan and integration doc by Friday EOD so we can share with Acme in the PoC kickoff.

Thanks,
Marissa
